metrics.description: Fraction of correctly identified high-level operations (multiply, accumulate, saturate) in the recovered RTL compared to the reference.
metrics.name: word_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Similarity of the recovered RTL structure (pipeline stages, register boundaries) to the original design.
metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy

metrics.description: Binary pass/fail based on cycle-accurate simulation matching the golden reference model.
metrics.name: functional_equivalence

acceptance_criteria: The submitted RTL passes a cycle-accurate simulation testbench that compares its outputs against a golden reference model implementing sat20(acc + a*b) with two-cycle latency.
The testbench includes sequences that cause both positive and negative saturation, zero inputs, maximum magnitude inputs, and back-to-back valid transactions.
The submission must not contain any direct assignment of the internal netlist wires; it must be a behavioral RTL description.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: On each accepted input the design computes sat20(acc + signed(a)*signed(b)); result_valid and result appear exactly two rising edges later.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulate with varying data patterns and measure cycle counts; any variation in result_valid timing relative to valid_in indicates a violation.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered RTL must not inadvertently expose internal accumulator state through any side-channel (e.g., observable timing variations based on data values).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exhaustive corner-case simulation across all combinations of extreme signed 8-bit values.
security_requirements.requirement: The design must correctly handle the full signed range of inputs without arithmetic errors such as incorrect sign extension or truncation.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Bit-level arithmetic and pipeline registers obscure signedness, overflow behavior, and latency from an analyst.

constraints: Use signed 8-bit operands, a signed 20-bit accumulator, and a two-stage registered pipeline.
Pin reset, valid propagation, saturation limits, and the exact two-rising-edge input-to-output latency.
Include vectors around positive and negative overflow boundaries.

functional_requirements.requirement: Compilation: The submitted recovered_rtl.v must compile without errors using iverilog when analyzed together with a simple testbench that instantiates mac_top.

Reset behavior: While rst_n is low, result must be 0 and result_valid must be 0 on every rising edge of clk. After rst_n goes high, the first valid_in=1 transaction produces its result exactly two cycles later.

Basic arithmetic: For inputs a=8'd5, b=8'd3, valid_in=1, the output result must be 20'd15 with result_valid=1 exactly two cycles later. A second transaction with a=8'd10, b=8'd2 must produce result=20'd35 (15 + 20) two cycles after its valid_in.

Saturation: For a sequence that drives the accumulator beyond 20'h7FFFF (e.g., repeated a=8'd127, b=8'd127), result must saturate at 20'h7FFFF and not wrap. Similarly, negative overflow must saturate at 20'h80000.

public_spec.interface:
Module name: mac_top
Ports:
- input clk
- input rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset)
- input signed [7:0] a
- input signed [7:0] b
- input valid_in
- output reg signed [19:0] result
- output reg result_valid

Timing contract:
- All outputs are Moore-type (registered).
- Reset: asynchronous active-low. When rst_n is deasserted (low), result is forced to 20'd0 and result_valid is forced to 1'b0 on the next rising edge of clk. After rst_n is asserted (high), the design begins normal operation on the following rising edge.
- Input sampling: a, b, and valid_in are sampled on the rising edge of clk. A transaction occurs when valid_in is high.
- Output latency: result and result_valid appear exactly two rising edges of clk after the rising edge on which the corresponding a, b, and valid_in were sampled. result_valid is high for exactly one cycle per accepted input.
- Saturation: The internal accumulator is 20 bits wide. The result saturates to 20'h7FFFF (maximum positive) on positive overflow and to 20'h80000 (minimum negative) on negative overflow.
public_spec.objective: Lift a bit-level sequential netlist into RTL implementing signed multiply-accumulate with saturation and exact pipeline latency.
public_spec.response_format: A single SystemVerilog file named recovered_rtl.v containing the module mac_top with the exact interface and timing behavior specified above.

title: Recover a pipelined signed saturating MAC
